_metadata.rubric: owner-clarified rubric with calibration anchors + no-literal-false-facts reminder, 2026-10-18
_metadata.independence: I read only u32-blind-input.json; no other repository file, search, web or paid API was used.

hints.reason: SHARK: the Jaws film's great white; WATER: the film's iconic beach/ocean scene and 'safe to go back in the water' tagline.
SHARK: the dorsal fin; WATER: the familiar scene of a fin cutting through the water (also swim fins).
SHARK: Shark Tank (TV show / aquarium shark tank); WATER: water tank compound.

best_available.why: Instant shark link and the film is defined by the ocean scene; strongest joint image.

pairs.pair_note: Healthy pair; all three hints work.

hints.reason: SHARK: lives in the sea; WITCH: 'sea witch' is a familiar phrase (Ursula is literally called the sea witch).
WITCH: Ursula the sea witch; SHARK: Ursula is an octopus-woman and her minions are eels, so there is no shark link.

best_available.why: Sea witch plus a sea creature reaches both cleanly.

pairs.pair_note: URSULA only reaches WITCH; do not explain it as a shark link.

hints.reason: SHARK: rows of famous teeth; WOLF: fangs, 'what big teeth you have' from Red Riding Hood.
Shared property: both are iconic apex predators (and both slang for predatory people: loan shark, wolf).
Shared property: both hunt prey, the wolf in packs and the shark alone.

best_available.why: The clearest shared category for both animals.

pairs.pair_note: HUNTER is close to PREDATOR; both are fine.

hints.reason: Shared property: snakes and spiders are the two classic phobias.
Shared property: both are known for venomous bites.
Shared action: snake bite and spider bite are both everyday phrases.

best_available.why: Most specific property the two share.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair.

hints.reason: SNAKE: snakes emerge from winter dormancy; SPRING: the season nature 'wakes', but neither side lands without explanation.
SNAKE: sheds its skin; SPRING: animals' spring shedding of winter coats is real but a weak route for most players.
SNAKE: a coiled snake; SPRING: a coil spring, a shared shape.

best_available.why: A shared shape anyone sees immediately.

pairs.pair_note: COIL carries the pair; WAKE and SHED depend on seasonal biology.

hints.reason: SNAKE: Latin for serpent; STAR: a real constellation, but few players know it.
SNAKE: the 'serpent-bearer'; STAR: a constellation / the '13th zodiac sign'. Factually sound but obscure on both sides.
SNAKE: sea snake; STAR: sea star (starfish), both compounds.

best_available.why: Two familiar compounds, no astronomy knowledge needed.

pairs.pair_note: The constellation hints are accurate but niche.

hints.reason: TRAIN: the toy train set; SNAKE: the rubber toy snake prank. Broad, but both phrases are familiar.
Shared verb: a snake winds along and a train winds through the hills, both long sinuous shapes.

best_available.why: Captures the shared long winding motion players already see between the two.

pairs.pair_note: WIND is the more pointed of the two; TOY is weaker on the snake side.

hints.reason: SNAKE: sea snake; WATER: sea water.
WATER: swimming is water-defined; SNAKE: snakes do swim but it is not a recognizable snake trait.
Compound 'water moccasin' is a snake (the cottonmouth), linking both at once; better known in the US.

best_available.why: The water moccasin is literally a water snake; the most pointed hint, SEA is the broader backup.

pairs.pair_note: MOCCASIN is US-leaning but a single compound that names both.

hints.reason: SNAKE: Medusa's hair of snakes; WITCH: she is a Gorgon, not a witch, so only a loose 'mythic villainess' link (calling her a witch would be wrong_fact).
WITCH: brewing potions; SNAKE: snake parts in the witches' brew ('fenny snake', 'adder's fork' in Macbeth) and snake oil, a real but second-hop route.

best_available.why: No false fact needed; the witch's brew with snake ingredients is a real image, while MEDUSA risks implying she is a witch.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Each hint is strong on one side only.

hints.reason: Shared story role: the serpent in Eden / Kaa and the Big Bad Wolf are archetypal villains (also 'snake in the grass', 'wolf in sheep's clothing').
Shared property: both are predators, literally and as words for predatory people.

best_available.why: Captures the shared storybook role, which is more pointed than the generic predator category.

pairs.pair_note: Both fine; PREDATOR is broader.

hints.reason: SPRING: to spring (verb) means to pounce; SPIDER: jumping/wolf spiders pounce on prey. Moderate on the spider side.
SPIDER: the jumping spider; SPRING: springing is jumping (verb route, springy).

best_available.why: Jumping spider is a familiar compound and 'spring' as a verb is jump.

pairs.pair_note: Both hints use the verb sense of SPRING.

hints.reason: SPIDER: eight legs; STAR: only via the radiating-points shape or a starfish's 'legs' (properly arms), a loose visual route.
SPIDER: spider web; STAR: no recognizable web route (the Webb telescope is a different spelling).
Contains the target SPIDER; the STAR route (film star / superhero) is weak anyway.

best_available.why: The only legal hint that reaches STAR at all, through the radiating shape.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; a 'sea'-style compound or shape hint is needed.

hints.reason: Contains the target SPIDER; the TRAIN route is the Spider-Man 2 train-stopping scene.
TRAIN: train tracks; SPIDER: no recognizable tracks link.

best_available.why: The only hint that does not contain a target, though it reaches TRAIN only.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; the real shared scene (Spider-Man 2 train) cannot be clued with the target word in it.

hints.reason: Shared story: the Itsy Bitsy Spider climbed up the water spout.

WATER: rain is water; SPIDER: 'down came the rain and washed the spider out' in the same rhyme.

hints.reason: Shared property: both are stock spooky Halloween figures.
Shared scene: spiders and witches are both core Halloween icons.
SPIDER: spins cobwebs; WITCH: only via the cobwebbed witch's lair / Halloween decor image.

pairs.pair_note: COBWEB leans to SPIDER.

hints.reason: Shared property: both are predators.

pairs.pair_note: Both are near-variants.

hints.reason: SPRING: spring bloom; STAR: no recognizable bloom route (star-named flowers are too far).
SPRING: spring training; STAR: 'star players train' is a story invented to rescue the word.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints reach SPRING only.

best_available.why: The only legal hint that reaches both, via the spring-training phrase.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; the natural clue TRAINING breaks the substring rule.

hints.reason: SPRING: spring rains / April showers; WATER: rainwater.
Compound: bottled spring water and bottled water.
SPRING: spring-fresh / fresh spring water; WATER: fresh water.

best_available.why: Points straight at the bottled spring water label.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair.

hints.reason: WITCH: the White Witch; SPRING: her endless winter breaks into spring as Aslan returns, a real plot point in the story.
WITCH: Walpurgis Night is the witches' night; SPRING: it is a 30 April spring festival. Accurate, but few players know it.

pairs.pair_note: NARNIA is moderate on the spring side; WALPURGIS is correct but obscure.

hints.reason: SPRING: to spring is to pounce (verb route); WOLF: a wolf pouncing on prey is a familiar image, moderately.

pairs.pair_note: Moderate pair; both hints need a beat of thought.

best_available.why: A night train under the stars is one recognizable scene.

pairs.pair_note: Thin pair; NIGHT is the moderate winner.

hints.reason: Shared scene: stars reflected on still water.
STAR: sea star (starfish); WATER: sea water.
STAR: 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star'; WATER: only loosely, as light sparkling on water.

pairs.pair_note: TWINKLE leans to STAR.

hints.reason: STAR: a five-pointed star; WITCH: the pentagram is the familiar witchcraft symbol.

WITCH: a witch's wand; STAR: the star-tipped wand, as carried by Glinda the Good Witch.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; every route is either niche, canine-not-wolf, or moon-not-star.

TRAIN: the Hogwarts Express; WITCH: Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry.
